t: Drexel Burnham Lambert files for bankruptcy
how: The main junk-bond dealer failed five months before the stock peak; high-yield default rates were rising towards 10%.

t: Fed cuts to 8.00%, three weeks before the invasion
how: The only cut until late October.
The business cycle peaked the same month; a recession ran from July 1990 to March 1991.
S&P 500 −1.1% to 351.48. Oil went from about $17 in July to $28 by 6 August.
−3.0% on the day and −16.8% from the peak. The highest VIX close of the whole decline.
Below the August low with the VIX lower. The index rose 1.7% the next session.
A lower price than August on less fear. Oil peaked near $46 in the same fortnight.
Fifth session after the low. The index closed above its 50-day average twelve sessions later.
S&P 500 −0.9% that day. The first cut since the invasion came 12 sessions after the low.

t: Corporate credit spread peaks at 2.45 points
how: Two months after the stock low, with the S&P 500 already 11.8% above it. Credit and earnings were still worsening while stocks rose.
The VIX fell to 27.5 from 36.2 three sessions earlier. The index closed above its 200-day average a week later.

t: NYSE breadth thrust: advances 2.17 times declines
how: Ten-day ratio by Deemer’s rule, about 80 sessions after the low and 19% above it.
Four months after the low and two weeks before the ground war.
